title: Dependency Auditing and Supply-Chain Awareness knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Dependency Auditing and Supply-Chain Awareness?
options: Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Enforce authorization on the server for every protected resource and keep secrets outside source control.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
questions.answer_key: Enforce authorization on the server for every protected resource and keep secrets outside source control.
questions.explanation: Enforce authorization on the server for every protected resource and keep secrets outside source control. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Dependency Auditing and Supply-Chain Awareness?
questions.explanation: “Security advisories” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Dependency Auditing and Supply-Chain Awareness implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
